brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: episodes as stars forming constellations creates instant emotional resonance and a memorable mental model
Cohesive cosmic palette — deep purples, warm yellows, soft cyan accents — supports the night-sky atmosphere convincingly
Restraint in chrome: floating transport pill and side legend keep the canvas as the hero
dominant_weaknesses: Constellations are visually scattered with weak grouping; you cannot tell which dots belong to which series without hovering
Color legend dots are tiny and the playing episode lacks any spatial anchor or pulse tying it to a star on the map
Now-playing block floats bottom-left disconnected from controls bottom-center, breaking reading flow and hierarchy
fix_priorities: Visually cluster each constellation with subtle connecting lines and tinted halos so series read as distinct shapes
Anchor the now-playing track to its glowing star (line, label, or zoom) to close the metaphor loop
Unify the bottom bar: align track metadata, controls, and a scrub timeline into one composed row
Increase legend dot size and add hover-highlight to filter constellations on the canvas
rationale.norman_balance: High visceral and reflective appeal from the celestial metaphor, but behavioral usability suffers — navigating episodes by star is ambiguous and slow.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes, the constellation metaphor is executed literally and poetically, though the interaction model for actually browsing episodes-as-stars needs more clarity to be functional.
